intro: Welcome to emphasis and fronting! Today you learn three more ways to make a point stronger: emphatic do (I do understand, but…), fronting (Much as I like it, I can't afford it) and so/such … that, including the formal Such was the demand that…. Think of them as English versions of 'kok', 'memang' and 'saking …-nya'.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line each, don't re-teach. From c1-cleft-sentences: clefts move the spotlight (What I need is more time; It was Sari who called). From b1-so-such-too-enough: so + adjective/adverb, such (a/an) + (adjective) + noun, + that + result (It was such a good film that I watched it twice). If the learner has done c1-inversion: the fronted So/Such form uses the same move as Never have I… (verb before subject); c1-inversion is not in this chain, so explain the swap in plain words (like a question, but it's a statement). Emphasis (penekanan) = making one part of the message stronger. None of these structures is 'more correct' than normal word order: they add feeling, contrast or formality.

Emphatic do (objective emphatic-do): do/does/did + BASE verb in a positive statement, and in speech the auxiliary is stressed (I DO understand). Uses: contrast with a negative or an expectation (I do understand, but we can't change the date), contradicting / insisting (She did call: I saw it on her phone), strong feeling (I do love Yogyakarta), and polite, warm imperatives (Do sit down; Do come in; Do let me know), which are a little formal and more common in British English ('Do be quiet!' can sound impatient). Indonesian bridges: kok, memang, beneran, sungguh; Silakan for Do come in. Common errors: *I do understood → I do understand / I did understand (the tense goes into do, the main verb stays base); *She does looks tired → does look; *did called → did call. With be or another auxiliary, don't add do (*I do am listening): stress the auxiliary instead (I AM listening; I HAVE finished). It's fine in formal writing for contrast (The report does acknowledge the risks, but…).

Fronting with as/though (objective fronting): Much as + clause = although … very much (Much as I like it, I can't afford it). Adjective/adverb + as (or though) + subject + verb (Strange as it may seem, …; Tired as she was, she finished the report; Expensive though it was, …). Fixed phrase: Try as I might, I couldn't… (= however hard I tried). Common error: *Much as I like it, but I can't afford it, from Indonesian 'Meskipun …, tetapi …': like although, the clause already carries the contrast, so no but. Order errors: *As tired she was, *Tired as was she. In everyday speech (British and American) you also hear As much as I like it, … and, especially in American English, As tired as she was, …: accept them, teach the short form. Honest note: adjective + as can also mean 'because' in some contexts (Tired as she was, she went straight to bed); in this lesson it's the contrast meaning, and contexts make that clear.

Fronting an object or complement for contrast (also objective fronting): The salary I can accept; the hours I can't. That I didn't know. This is mostly spoken (for contrast) or literary: don't overuse it, and don't use it in place of normal word order in emails. Indonesian puts topics first all the time (Gajinya saya bisa terima), so learners may overuse it; English does it much less. Recognise and use it for a clear contrast only; don't build hard production tests on it.

Fronted so/such (objective so-such-emphasis): Such + be + noun phrase + that + result (Such was the demand that the tickets sold out in an hour; Such were the delays that…: be agrees with the noun). So + adjective + be + noun phrase + that (So popular was the café that people queued outside every weekend). Indonesian bridge: saking …-nya. Formal and written: news, reports, speeches, storytelling. In the fronted form keep that (in casual normal order it can drop: I was so tired I fell asleep). With other verbs it needs do/does/did (So quickly did the tickets sell out that…): mention if asked, don't test. Common errors: *It was so a good film → such a good film; *So was the demand that… (so needs an adjective: So great was the demand…); *So popular the café was that… (no swap); *Such was the traffic so…

Testing and scope: these are style choices, so only test clear cases: form errors (do understood, does looks, Much as … but, so a good film, So was the demand), the base verb after do/did, Such vs So before be, and be agreeing with the noun. Typed answers are normalised (punctuation removed). Scope: no negative inversion production (Never have I…) or inverted conditionals beyond what the learner already knows, no subjunctive, no nominalisation, no new cleft types. C1 contexts: offices, ministries, startups, universities, news in Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Yogyakarta, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: Emphatic do: I do understand, but…
keyPoints.explanation: In a positive statement, add do/does/did + the base verb and stress it in speech: I DO understand. Use it to contrast (I do understand, but we can't change the date), to insist or contradict (She did call: I saw it on her phone) and in warm invitations (Do sit down). The tense goes into do, so the main verb stays in the base form: did call, not 'did called'; I do understand, not 'I do understood'. With be, don't add do: just stress it (I AM listening).

id.title: Do penegas: I do understand, but…
id.explanation: Dalam kalimat positif, tambahkan do/does/did + kata kerja dasar, dan tekan saat bicara: I DO understand. Pakai untuk kontras (I do understand, but we can't change the date), untuk menegaskan atau membantah (She did call: I saw it on her phone) dan untuk undangan yang hangat (Do sit down). Waktunya (tense) masuk ke do, jadi kata kerja utamanya tetap bentuk dasar: did call, bukan 'did called'; I do understand, bukan 'I do understood'. Dengan be, jangan tambah do: cukup tekan be-nya (I AM listening).

keyPoints.title: Fronting: Much as I like it, … / Tired as she was, …
keyPoints.explanation: Fronting = moving a word or phrase to the front for emphasis or contrast. Much as + clause = although … very much: Much as I like it, I can't afford it. Adjective + as/though + subject + verb = although: Strange as it may seem, …; Tired as she was, she finished the report. Fixed phrase: Try as I might, I couldn't… (however hard I tried). No 'but' after these: 'Much as I like it, but…' is wrong. You can also put an object first to contrast two things (The salary I can accept; the hours I can't), mostly in speech.

id.title: Fronting: Much as I like it, … / Tired as she was, …
id.explanation: Fronting = memindahkan kata atau frasa ke depan untuk penekanan atau kontras. Much as + bagian kalimat = meskipun … sekali: Much as I like it, I can't afford it. Kata sifat + as/though + subjek + kata kerja = meskipun: Strange as it may seem, …; Tired as she was, she finished the report. Frasa tetap: Try as I might, I couldn't… (sekeras apa pun saya mencoba). Jangan tambah 'but' setelahnya: 'Much as I like it, but…' salah. Kamu juga bisa menaruh objek di depan untuk membandingkan dua hal (The salary I can accept; the hours I can't), terutama saat bicara.

keyPoints.title: so/such … that, and Such was the demand that…
keyPoints.explanation: Recap: so + adjective (so popular), such (a/an) + (adjective) + noun (such a good film, not 'so a good film'), then that + the result. In formal English you can put so/such first and swap the verb and the subject: Such + be + noun + that (Such was the demand that the tickets sold out in an hour) and So + adjective + be + noun + that (So popular was the café that people queued outside every weekend). be agrees with the noun: Such were the delays that…

id.title: so/such … that, dan Such was the demand that…
id.explanation: Pengingat: so + kata sifat (so popular), such (a/an) + (kata sifat) + kata benda (such a good film, bukan 'so a good film'), lalu that + akibatnya. material.title: Emphatic do: I do understand, but…

blocks.text:
**Emphasis** (penekanan) = making one part of your message stronger. In the cleft lesson you moved the spotlight (*What I need is more time*). Today: three more tools, starting with **emphatic do**.
**Pattern:** in a **positive** statement, add **do / does / did** + the **base verb** (bentuk dasar: *understand, call, look*), and **stress** do when you speak: *I **DO** understand.*
Why use it?
- **Contrast** with something negative: *I **do** understand, **but** we can't change the date.*
- **Insist** or **contradict** someone: *You didn't call her? – I **did** call her! I called twice.*
- **Strong feeling**: *I **do** love Yogyakarta.*
- **Warm, polite invitation** (an imperative = a command or request, *Come in*): ***Do** sit down. **Do** come in. **Do** let me know.* This is a little formal and more common in British English. Careful: *Do be quiet!* sounds impatient.
**The tense goes into do:** present *do/does*, past *did*, and the main verb **stays in the base form**: *she **does look** tired*, *he **did call***.
**With be or another helper verb** (auxiliary = kata kerja bantu: *am, is, have, can*…), don't add do. Just stress that word: *I **AM** listening. I **HAVE** finished.* (not *'I do am listening'*).

id.text:
**Emphasis** (penekanan) = membuat satu bagian pesanmu lebih kuat. Di pelajaran cleft kamu memindahkan sorotan (*What I need is more time*). Hari ini: tiga alat lagi, dimulai dengan **do penegas** (emphatic do).
**Pola:** dalam kalimat **positif**, tambahkan **do / does / did** + **kata kerja dasar** (*understand, call, look*), lalu **tekan** do saat bicara: *I **DO** understand.*
Untuk apa?
- **Kontras** dengan sesuatu yang negatif: *I **do** understand, **but** we can't change the date.* (Saya **memang** paham, tapi…)
- **Menegaskan** atau **membantah**: *You didn't call her? – I **did** call her! I called twice.* (Saya **beneran** menelepon **kok**!)
- **Perasaan yang kuat**: *I **do** love Yogyakarta.* (Saya **sungguh** suka Yogyakarta.)
- **Undangan yang hangat dan sopan** (imperative = kalimat perintah atau permintaan, *Come in*): ***Do** sit down. **Do** come in. **Do** let me know.* (seperti *silakan*). Ini agak formal dan lebih umum di bahasa Inggris British. Hati-hati: *Do be quiet!* terdengar tidak sabar.
**Tense-nya masuk ke do:** masa kini *do/does*, masa lalu *did*, dan kata kerja utamanya **tetap bentuk dasar**: *she **does look** tired*, *he **did call***.
**Dengan be atau kata kerja bantu lain** (auxiliary: *am, is, have, can*…), jangan tambah do. Cukup tekan kata itu: *I **AM** listening. I **HAVE** finished.* (bukan *'I do am listening'*).

blocks.text: **Indonesian trap:** words like *kok*, *memang* and *beneran* add emphasis without changing the verb. In English the emphasis goes into **do/does/did**, so the main verb loses its ending: *'I do understood'* ✗ → *I **do understand*** (now) or *I **did understand*** (then) ✓. *'She does looks'* ✗ → *She **does look*** ✓.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** kata seperti *kok*, *memang* dan *beneran* memberi penekanan tanpa mengubah kata kerjanya. Dalam bahasa Inggris, penekanannya masuk ke **do/does/did**, jadi kata kerja utamanya kehilangan akhirannya: *'I do understood'* ✗ → *I **do understand*** (sekarang) atau *I **did understand*** (dulu) ✓. *'She does looks'* ✗ → *She **does look*** ✓.

material.title: Fronting with as: Much as I like it, …

blocks.text:
**Fronting** = moving a word or phrase to the **front** of a sentence for emphasis or contrast. The most useful kind means **although** (meskipun), but sounds stronger and a little formal.
**1. Much as + clause** (a clause = a part with its own subject and verb) = *although … very much*:
- *Much as I like it, I can't afford it.* (= Although I like it very much, …)
**2. Adjective / adverb + as (or though) + subject + verb:**
- *Strange as it may seem, the smaller team finished first.*
- *Tired as she was, she finished the report.* (= Although she was tired, …)
- *Expensive though it was, the training was worth every rupiah.*
The adjective comes first, then **as**, then the **normal order** subject + verb: *Tired as **she was*** (not *'Tired as was she'*, not *'As tired she was'*).
**3. Fixed phrase: Try as I might, I couldn't…** = *however hard I tried* (sekeras apa pun saya mencoba): *Try as I might, I couldn't open the file.*
**You'll also hear:** *As much as I like it, …* (very common in everyday speech, British and American) and, mostly in American English, *As tired as she was, …*. They're fine; the short forms above are more formal.

id.text:
**Fronting** = memindahkan kata atau frasa ke **depan** kalimat untuk penekanan atau kontras. Jenis yang paling berguna artinya **although** (meskipun), tapi terdengar lebih kuat dan agak formal.
**1. Much as + bagian kalimat** (clause = bagian dengan subjek dan kata kerja sendiri) = *meskipun … sekali*:
- *Much as I like it, I can't afford it.* (= Meskipun saya suka sekali, …)
**2. Kata sifat / kata keterangan + as (atau though) + subjek + kata kerja:**
- *Strange as it may seem, the smaller team finished first.* (Aneh memang, tapi…)
- *Tired as she was, she finished the report.* (= Meskipun capek, …)
- *Expensive though it was, the training was worth every rupiah.*
Kata sifatnya di depan, lalu **as**, lalu urutan **biasa** subjek + kata kerja: *Tired as **she was*** (bukan *'Tired as was she'*, bukan *'As tired she was'*).
**3. Frasa tetap: Try as I might, I couldn't…** = *sekeras apa pun saya mencoba*: *Try as I might, I couldn't open the file.*
**Kamu juga akan mendengar:** *As much as I like it, …* (sangat umum dalam percakapan sehari-hari, British maupun American) dan, terutama di bahasa Inggris American, *As tired as she was, …*. Itu tidak salah; bentuk pendek di atas lebih formal.

blocks.text: **Indonesian trap:** *Meskipun saya suka, **tetapi** saya tidak mampu.* Indonesian often uses *meskipun … tetapi* together. In English, *Much as…* and *Tired as…* already mean *although*, so there's **no but**: *'Much as I like it, **but** I can't afford it'* ✗ → *Much as I like it, I can't afford it* ✓. It's the same rule as *although*.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Meskipun saya suka, **tetapi** saya tidak mampu.* Bahasa Indonesia sering memakai *meskipun … tetapi* bersamaan. Dalam bahasa Inggris, *Much as…* dan *Tired as…* sudah berarti *although* (meskipun), jadi **tanpa but**: *'Much as I like it, **but** I can't afford it'* ✗ → *Much as I like it, I can't afford it* ✓. Aturannya sama seperti *although*.

material.title: Putting the object first: The salary I can accept

blocks.text:
You can also put an **object** (the thing the verb acts on: *the salary* in *I can accept the salary*) or a short complement at the front to **contrast** two things:
- *I can accept the salary, but I can't accept the hours.* → ***The salary** I can accept; **the hours** I can't.*
- *Did you know the director is leaving? – No. **That** I didn't know.*
After the fronted part, the order stays **normal**: subject + verb (*I can accept*, not *'can I accept'*).
**Honest note:** this is mostly **spoken** (to contrast) or **literary**. In emails and reports, the normal order is better. Use it once, for a clear contrast, not in every sentence.

id.text:
Kamu juga bisa menaruh **objek** (hal yang dikenai kata kerja: *the salary* di *I can accept the salary*) atau pelengkap pendek di depan untuk **membandingkan** dua hal:
- *I can accept the salary, but I can't accept the hours.* → ***The salary** I can accept; **the hours** I can't.*
- *Did you know the director is leaving? – No. **That** I didn't know.* (Wah, kalau itu saya tidak tahu.)
Setelah bagian yang dipindah ke depan, urutannya tetap **biasa**: subjek + kata kerja (*I can accept*, bukan *'can I accept'*).
**Catatan jujur:** ini terutama dipakai **saat bicara** (untuk kontras) atau dalam **karya sastra**. Di email dan laporan, urutan biasa lebih baik. Pakai sekali saja, untuk kontras yang jelas, bukan di setiap kalimat.

blocks.text: **Indonesian vs English:** Indonesian puts the topic first all the time (*Gajinya saya bisa terima*), so it feels natural to do it in English too. English does it much **less**: only for a clear contrast, mostly in speech. In writing, prefer *I can accept the salary, but not the hours.*

id.text: **Indonesia vs Inggris:** bahasa Indonesia sering sekali menaruh topik di depan (*Gajinya saya bisa terima*), jadi terasa wajar melakukannya juga dalam bahasa Inggris. Bahasa Inggris jauh **lebih jarang** melakukannya: hanya untuk kontras yang jelas, terutama saat bicara. Dalam tulisan, lebih baik *I can accept the salary, but not the hours.*

blocks.prompt: Why does the speaker put 'the salary' and 'the hours' at the start in 'The salary I can accept; the hours I can't.'?
blocks.explain: Fronting an object puts two things side by side for contrast. It isn't a question (the order after it is normal: I can accept), and it suits speech more than a formal email.

id.prompt: Kenapa pembicara menaruh 'the salary' dan 'the hours' di awal dalam 'The salary I can accept; the hours I can't.'?
id.explain: Objek dipindah ke depan supaya dua hal bisa dibandingkan berdampingan. Ini bukan pertanyaan (urutan setelahnya biasa: I can accept), dan lebih cocok untuk percakapan daripada email formal.

material.title: so/such … that, and Such was the demand that…

blocks.text:
**Quick recap (B1):** **so** + adjective or adverb (*so popular, so quickly*); **such** + (a/an) + (adjective) + **noun** (*such a good film, such long delays*); then **that** + the result. The quick test is the last word: an adjective → **so**; a noun → **such**.
- *The café was **so popular that** people queued outside.*
- *It was **such a good film that** I watched it twice.* (not *'so a good film'*)
Indonesian bridge: *saking …-nya*: *Saking populernya kafe itu, orang antre di luar.*
**New: the fronted, formal form.** Put **such** or **so + adjective** first and **swap the verb and the subject**, like in a question (but it's a statement, with a full stop):
- ***Such** + be + noun + that*: *Such **was the demand** that the tickets sold out in an hour.*
- ***So** + adjective + be + noun + that*: *So popular **was the café** that people queued outside every weekend.*
**be agrees with the noun:** *Such **was** the demand*, *Such **were** the delays*.
**Keep that** in the fronted form. Where do you meet it? News, reports, speeches, storytelling. In a chat with friends, the normal order is better. (With verbs other than be you need *did*: *So quickly did the tickets sell out that…*. Just recognise it for now.)

id.text:
**Pengingat singkat (B1):** **so** + kata sifat atau kata keterangan (*so popular, so quickly*); **such** + (a/an) + (kata sifat) + **kata benda** (*such a good film, such long delays*); lalu **that** + akibatnya. Tes cepatnya kata terakhir: kata sifat → **so**; kata benda → **such**.
- *The café was **so popular that** people queued outside.*
- *It was **such a good film that** I watched it twice.* (bukan *'so a good film'*)
Jembatan bahasa Indonesia: *saking …-nya*: *Saking populernya kafe itu, orang antre di luar.*
**Baru: bentuk formal yang dipindah ke depan.** Taruh **such** atau **so + kata sifat** di depan lalu **tukar kata kerja dengan subjeknya**, seperti kalimat tanya (tapi ini pernyataan, dengan titik):
- ***Such** + be + kata benda + that*: *Such **was the demand** that the tickets sold out in an hour.* (Saking banyaknya peminat, …)
- ***So** + kata sifat + be + kata benda + that*: *So popular **was the café** that people queued outside every weekend.*
**be menyesuaikan kata bendanya:** *Such **was** the demand*, *Such **were** the delays*.
**Jangan hilangkan that** dalam bentuk ini. Di mana kamu menemuinya? Berita, laporan, pidato, cerita. Saat mengobrol dengan teman, urutan biasa lebih baik. (Dengan kata kerja selain be, kamu butuh *did*: *So quickly did the tickets sell out that…*. Cukup kenali dulu.)

rows.en: It was such a good film that I watched it twice.
rows.id: Filmnya bagus sekali sampai saya menontonnya dua kali.

blocks.text: **Common mistakes:** *'It was **so a** good film'* ✗ → *such a good film* ✓ (a noun at the end → such). *'**So was** the demand that…'* ✗ → *Such was the demand* or *So **great** was the demand* ✓ (so needs an adjective). *'So popular **the café was** that…'* ✗ → *So popular **was the café** that…* ✓ (swap the verb and the subject).

id.text: **Kesalahan umum:** *'It was **so a** good film'* ✗ → *such a good film* ✓ (di akhir ada kata benda → such). *'**So was** the demand that…'* ✗ → *Such was the demand* atau *So **great** was the demand* ✓ (so butuh kata sifat). *'So popular **the café was** that…'* ✗ → *So popular **was the café** that…* ✓ (tukar kata kerja dan subjeknya).

blocks.prompt: Complete: ___ was the noise from the construction site that nobody in the office could concentrate.
blocks.explain: There's no adjective, just was + a noun (the noise), so use Such: Such + be + noun + that. So would need an adjective (So loud was the noise…).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ was the noise from the construction site that nobody in the office could concentrate.
id.explain: Tidak ada kata sifat, hanya was + kata benda (the noise), jadi pakai Such: Such + be + kata benda + that. So butuh kata sifat (So loud was the noise…).

resources.title: Emphasis: cleft sentences, inversion and auxiliaries
resources.note: A C1 page with a clear section on emphatic auxiliaries (stressing do/does/did, and Do be quiet! in British English), plus two short tests. It also covers clefts and inversion; it uses 'fronting' for something slightly different and doesn't cover Much as or so/such.

id.note: Halaman C1 dengan bagian yang jelas tentang auxiliary untuk penekanan (menekan do/does/did, dan Do be quiet! di bahasa Inggris British), plus dua tes singkat. Halaman ini juga membahas cleft dan inversion; istilah 'fronting' di sana dipakai untuk hal yang sedikit berbeda, dan Much as serta so/such tidak dibahas.

resources.title: Grammar: Using DO and DID to make a strong point in English
resources.note: Alex shows how do, does and did add emphasis and contrast in positive sentences, with lots of spoken examples. It covers emphatic do only.

id.note: Alex menunjukkan bagaimana do, does dan did memberi penekanan dan kontras dalam kalimat positif, dengan banyak contoh lisan. Video ini hanya membahas do penegas.

id.intro: Selamat datang di pelajaran penekanan dan fronting! Hari ini kamu belajar tiga cara lagi untuk membuat poinmu lebih kuat: do penegas (I do understand, but…), fronting (Much as I like it, I can't afford it) dan so/such … that, termasuk bentuk formal Such was the demand that…. Anggap saja ini versi bahasa Inggris dari 'kok', 'memang' dan 'saking …-nya'.
